entry_state: Chapter4 concludes with an integration proposal rather than an established originality or empirical claim. Chapter5 selects a shared typed IR, retains SQL/Python as the serious comparator, and bounds each inspected reuse component. Chapter6 now defines model-relative historical compatibility through contextual observations and joint constraints; empty, singleton and larger families have distinct interpretations. Section6.1 is complete; certain-answer semantics follows.

findings.judgment: A100 payable exists in both declared histories despite the empty intersection of creditor rows; their union would double count it. Nonempty-family certainty, sampled answers and solver inconclusiveness retain distinct meanings. Libkin theorem conditions and SQL restrictions are stated rather than transferred to financial computation.

The null-space construction holds only when both histories satisfy the remaining constraints. Identical movements can still conceal reset terms. The signed-ledger induction establishes balance, not account eligibility or contract existence; reports require movements and contract state as well as balances.

exit_state: The payable example distinguishes possible answer schedules, individually certain rows and universally true propositions. Relational theorems retain their input/output assumptions and do not certify arbitrary financial queries. Null-space ambiguity and the receivables bridge show why reports cannot identify all movements or contract terms. A balanced signed ledger preserves bookkeeping conservation, while reports also need classified movements, economic state, basis and perimeter. Sections6.2–6.4 are complete; event generation follows.
